title: The small fitting on an outdoor faucet is a hose-bib vacuum breaker
description: Identify the threaded hose-connection device, understand its drain and anti-siphon function, and avoid damaging a non-removable model.
prompt: What is the faucet attachment doing?
answer: A hose-bib vacuum breaker protects against backsiphonage at a hose connection. Brief drainage after shutoff differs from continuous leaking or a damaged diaphragm.
urgency: Do not defeat a break-away set screw or remove a non-removable device without confirming the faucet and local requirement.
diagramAlt: Outdoor faucet with threaded hose-bib vacuum breaker, drain openings, and hose connection
identifiers: Female hose thread attaches to the faucet; male hose thread accepts the hose.
Small side or bottom openings can drain when pressure changes.
Some models use a break-away screw to become non-removable.

choices.label: It sprays only when the faucet shuts off
choices.detail: Brief drain-down may be part of operation; record duration.

choices.label: It leaks continuously while on
choices.detail: A worn or fouled internal seal may need model-specific service or replacement.

choices.label: I want to remove it
choices.detail: First check for a break-away screw and why the device was required.

steps.title: Confirm the fitting
steps.body: Look for hose threads, vent openings, brand, and a set-screw location.

steps.title: Observe on and off cycles
steps.body: Separate shutoff drainage from continuous pressurized leakage.

steps.title: Match the replacement
steps.body: Use the correct thread, pressure use, approval, and drain feature.

safeChecks: Remove the hose and observe the faucet attachment.
Photograph the set screw before any work.
stopConditions: The device is seized and the faucet piping twists
notThisDevice: A PVB is a larger raised assembly with test cocks.
An AVB is installed in piping rather than on hose threads.
A pressure regulator has no atmospheric drain openings.
evidenceNote: Product instructions and local inspection requirements determine whether a hose-connection device may be removed or replaced.
